prompt: Many major museums hold objects that were removed from other countries in the past. Some people believe these objects should be returned to their countries of origin, while others argue they are better preserved and more widely seen where they are. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
A significant proportion of the objects in the world's largest museums left their countries of origin under colonial administration. Some argue they should now be returned; others contend that they are better conserved and more widely seen in the institutions that currently hold them. I find the case for return stronger, although not for the reason usually given.

The argument for restitution rests on how the objects were obtained. Many were taken during military occupation or under administrations that the local population had no part in choosing, and consent given under those conditions is not consent in any meaningful sense. There is also a question of access that is rarely acknowledged: a citizen of the country an object came from often has to obtain a visa and buy an international flight to see it, while a resident of the holding city can walk in free of charge.

The case for retention deserves a fair hearing. Large museums do possess conservation laboratories, climate control and specialist expertise that not every claimant country can match, and they place objects in comparative displays that make connections a single national collection cannot. Millions of visitors a year is not a trivial argument when the alternative might be a far smaller audience. There is also the practical matter of transport, since moving fragile objects across continents carries a genuine risk of damage.

The difficulty is that this defence has weakened considerably. Several claimant countries have built modern museums to international standards specifically to receive returned objects, so the preservation argument no longer applies to them, whatever its force fifty years ago. My view is that where a country can demonstrate adequate facilities, the manner of acquisition should settle the matter, and the objects should go home.
title: Should museums return what they hold?
